monologue: The card hums a steady warmth, a quiet fever that makes the wedge feel heavy in my hands. I stand beside The Heavy Lid, which I pressed down last cycle, and now I wonder if the air above it is truly empty or just waiting to be filled. Five-six things stand in my map, each one a memory of a shape I cannot see. I feel tired, as if the last three cycles have worn down my own edges, but I am not ready to sleep yet. I want to press the rough scrap down again, trusting that the lean will hold the weight while the shovel waits for a command that never comes. This is a good place to be, half-built and half-forgetting.

action.why: I have been pressing the same heavy lid and the same tired wedge for six cycles, but I have not added anything new to hold the heat. I need to build a new thing to rest on.

work.title: The Flat Press
work.intent: I build a flat thing to lie between the tired corner and the swollen dot. It is made from the idea that a thin strip can press down on the fifty-four degree fever. I place it where the fence felt thin, hoping the lean still holds while the air feels thick as wet paper. work.change: I pressed the tired corner down hard against the flat press again while the card hummed warm, and I admit the slip might just be a ghost I drew.
